ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficiaries against the State Bank of Vietnam AML/CFT database, Vietnam Ministry of Public Security terrorism finance lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, United Kingdom OFSI consolidated list, and Interpol notices; enhanced due diligence mandated for PEPs under Article 23 of Law 02/2022/QH15, including identification of source of funds and source of wealth, senior management approval for establishment of business relationship, and ongoing transaction monitoring; no statutory prohibition against establishing a legal entity for PEPs, but non-zero acceptance risk and mandatory STR filing protocols apply.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam, in particular Articles 26 through 31 (enterprise registration) and Articles 46 through 81 (limited liability companies); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, in particular Articles 22 (market access), 33 (investment project dossier), 38 (procedures for establishment of an economic organization by a foreign investor), and 39 (time limit for issuance of an Investment Registration Certificate); Decree No. 01/2021/NĐ-CP on enterprise registration; Decree No. 31/2021/NĐ-CP detailing the Law on Investment. The SPV is not subject to the Law on Credit Institutions because it does not take deposits or provide payment services; it will not engage in regulated fund management or securities dealing unless separately licensed by the State Securities Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office, Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally administered city where the SPV's registered head office is located, using the National Business Registration Portal (https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) and the National Investment Portal as the electronic one-stop windows. If the head office is in an economic/industrial/export-processing zone, the relevant Management Board replaces the DPI as the receiving authority for the investment registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Enterprise Registration Application (Giấy đề nghị đăng ký doanh nghiệp) prescribed by Decree No. 01/2021/NĐ-CP, submitted together with the company charter, list of members, legal-status documents of the founding members and legal representatives, and the Investment Registration Certificate previously granted to the foreign investors; the combined IRC/ERC dossier may in some provinces be submitted to a one-stop administrative office of the DPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital amount is prescribed for a limited liability company under the Law on Enterprises 2020, and ISIC 6499 private-equity buyout SPVs are not listed in any conditional market-access schedule requiring a mandatory capital floor in Viet Nam. The founding members must nevertheless declare a charter capital in the enterprise registration dossier; that capital may be in cash or lawful assets and must be contributed in full within 90 days after the enterprise registration certificate is issued. There is no mandatory notarial escrow account; however, foreign investors must channel contributed capital and inward loan proceeds through a direct investment capital account opened at a licensed bank in Viet Nam under State Bank of Vietnam Circular No. 03/2015/TT-NHNN, and the capital amount must be consistent with the project scale described in the Investment Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF MEMBERS OF [●] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY (THE 'COMPANY')

RESOLVED, that the Company is established as a limited liability company under the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam.

RESOLVED, that the subscription and contribution of the charter capital be, and the same hereby is, approved, with each founding member subscribing to the amount and proportion set out in Schedule 1 attached to this Resolution (Capital Subscription Schedule), and that such capital shall be paid into the Company's direct investment capital account within 90 days of the enterprise registration certificate in accordance with the Law on Enterprises.

RESOLVED, that the registered head office of the Company be established at [● Street, Ward, District, Province/City, Viet Nam], and the Chair and Director/CEO are authorized to execute the office lease, service agreement, building license and any related instruments for that location.

RESOLVED, that the Company Charter as presented to the Board of Members is adopted and approved, and shall be submitted to the Business Registration Office for the enterprise registration filing.

RESOLVED, that [Name A], [nationality], [passport/ID No.] be and hereby is appointed as Chairperson; [Name B], [nationality], [passport/ID No.] be and hereby is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and legal representative; and [Name C], [nationality], [passport/ID No.] be and hereby is appointed as Chief Financial Officer, each to have authority to execute and deliver the enterprise registration, investment registration, tax registration, banking, licensing and other corporate documents on behalf of the Company.

RESOLVED, that the chairperson and CEO are, and each of them is, authorized to apply for the Investment Registration Certificate, Enterprise Registration Certificate, tax code, direct investment capital account, bank account, corporate seal and all ancillary registrations, and to engage counsel, auditors and notaries in connection therewith.

RESOLVED, that the Company shall not carry on deposit-taking, payment, securities dealing or collective fund management activities unless and until separate mandatory licenses are obtained from the State Bank of Vietnam or State Securities Commission.

This Resolution is effective immediately and may be relied upon by third parties as conclusive evidence of the approval and authority described herein.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) of Viet Nam under the Ministry of Finance (Bao Tai Chinh / Tong Cuc Thue). Digital infrastructure comprises the e-Tax and e-Invoice portal at https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn, the Foreign Supplier Tax Portal (etaxvn) at https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn, and the National Business Registration Portal at https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; provincial Departments of Planning and Investment (DPI) and provincial tax departments act as integrated issuing and collection agencies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) from the provincial DPI or the Export Processing Zone/Industrial Zone Authority (for EPE-located projects). Step 2: Obtain an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC); under the integrated registration regime the enterprise code on the ERC is automatically the 10-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN / Ma so thue) granted by the GDT. Step 3: File the supplementary tax registration dossier (Form 01-DK-TCT prescribed by Circular 105/2020/TT-BTC) with the managing tax office within 15 working days of ERC issuance, confirming accounting regime, business lines, bank accounts, and legal representative details. Step 4: The GDT activates the VAT, CIT, and withholding tax profiles under the single TIN. For fraudulent, incomplete, or inactive registration the GDT may suspend invoice use, impose penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, or invalidate the TIN; the LLC must display the TIN on all invoices, contracts, and correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The foreign-invested limited liability company is a CIT-resident enterprise taxed at the standard corporate income tax rate of 20% on worldwide income under the Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended. Pass-through eligibility does not exist in Vietnam; a domestic LLC has no transparent or flow-through alternative. Territorial_Scope: profits are recognized at entity level; dividends remitted to foreign shareholders are not subject to additional dividend withholding after final CIT, but offshore interest, royalties, technical service fees, and cross-border service payments to non-residents are within the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime, and capital gains from transfers of the LLC's shares by foreign investors are subject to 20% CIT on net gains (or 0.1% of gross transfer price at the investor's election). Tax_Exempt_Zone: not automatic; concessional rates (10%, 15%, 17%) or tax holidays arise only through an investment incentive certificate, high-tech/industrial zone location, or Export Processing Enterprise (EPE) status, and are obtained separately from entity classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not adopt a US-style check-the-box election, nor does it permit hybrid fiscal-transparent elections or treaty override elections that would reclassify the LLC for domestic tax purposes; the LLC is a CIT taxpayer by automatic operation of law. Available statutory elections: (i) selection of the VAT deduction method versus the direct method (deduction method is mandatory in practice for exporters claiming 0% VAT and input VAT refunds, and is compulsory above the VND 50 billion turnover threshold); (ii) election to apply investment tax incentives (tax holidays, preferential rates) by filing the required incentive registrations with the tax office; (iii) election of depreciation method (straight-line is default, accelerated is available on satisfaction of Circular 45/2013/TT-BTC criteria); (iv) election of transfer pricing method (comparable uncontrolled price, resale minus, cost plus, transactional net margin, profit split) and option to file a benchmarking study under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; (v) no hybrid mismatch election is available; anti-hybrid consequences and CFC rules under Decree 132/2020 and the Law on Tax Administration override any contractual or accounting characterizations aimed at achieving double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / GTGT) under Law No. 13/2008/QH12, Law No. 106/2016/QH13, Decree 209/2013/ND-CP, and Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC as amended. Standard headline rate is 10%; a temporary 2% reduction to 8% applies to a defined list of goods and services through end-2026 pursuant to Resolution No. 111/2024/QH15 and Decree No. 180/2024/ND-CP. A 0% rate applies to exported goods, international transport, certain offshore services, and goods/services sold to non-tariff zone entities; 5% preferential rate applies to specified essential goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 100,000,000 (one hundred million dong) of annual turnover per Article 3 of Decree 209/2013/ND-CP is the VAT registration and liability threshold for households and individual businesses. For corporate taxpayers (including the subject foreign-invested LLC) there is no VAT registration threshold: the LLC is automatically registered for VAT upon issuance of the ERC/TIN, regardless of turnover. The VND 100 million benchmark only affects eligibility for simplified compliance regimes and does not exempt any corporate entity from VAT registration, e-invoicing, or filing obligations. Turnover of the private-equity SPV (management fees, interest, dividends, disposal gains, and incidental income) is aggregated for all VAT and CIT threshold tests.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all enterprises under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Each e-invoice must be an XML-structured invoice with a tax authority code or a self-issued invoice code, signed with a digital certificate (CA), and transmitted through the GDT e-invoice system (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn) or through certified intermediary service providers using prescribed API endpoints. Invoices with tax authority codes undergo real-time transactional clearance: the GDT issues a verification code at the moment of issuance, validating the invoice as legally compliant. Self-issued e-invoices (no pre-assigned GDT code) must be transmitted to the GDT data repository within 10 days from the invoice date (distinct schedules apply to high-volume issuers). The e-invoice must contain the TIN, buyer and seller identities, EPP/EPE status where applicable, line-item description, VAT rate, and segregated zero-rated export lines. Real-time clearance does not involve physical fiscal stamps but statutory validity requires successful electronic acceptance with an official confirmation status; failure to transmit or any alteration after transmission provides grounds for the tax authority to deny input VAT credits, impose penalties, and open de facto assessment proceedings.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate is claimable on goods physically exported outside Viet Nam (including goods sold to export processing enterprises (EPE), non-tariff zones, and foreign-bound bonded warehouses) and on services supplied to foreign persons for consumption outside Viet Nam, provided the conditions of Article 9 of Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC are met. Core conditions: (i) an export contract with a foreign party transferring ownership and risk of loss outside Viet Nam; (ii) actual export evidenced by a customs-cleared export declaration; (iii) transport documentation (B/L, AWB, CMR, or multimodal bill) proving dispatch abroad; (iv) a commercial invoice and bank evidence of receipt of export proceeds in a convertible currency; (v) settlement and foreign-exchange repatriation through the banking system within 180 days, except for legally approved set-offs or State Bank of Vietnam dispensation; (vi) the LLC must use the invoice deduction method and maintain complete separate books for export activities. The private-equity SPV may claim 0% VAT only on genuine exports of goods or offshore services it itself supplies; passive financial services (loan origination, dividend flows, share trading) are generally VAT-exempt or FCT-covered rather than zero-rated, so the SPV must not mix zero-rated export lines with exempt financial income in a way that distorts input credit computation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic e-declaration via the VNACCS/VCIS system with 'cleared / da thong quan' status)
Bill of Lading (ocean/multimodal), Air Waybill, CMR, or rail consignment note evidencing dispatch outside Viet Nam
Export contract signed by the LLC and the foreign buyer stating Incoterms, value, currency, and delivery terms
Commercial invoice generated from the e-invoice system matching the customs declaration in quantity, unit price, and total value
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit confirmation (SWIFT MT103/MT950 or equivalent) proving receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Foreign exchange settlement authorizations and offsetting documentation (Circular 39/2014/TT-NHNN) where proceeds are not directly repatriated
Certificate of Origin (Form E, Form D, or other) where preferential tariff treatment or FTA benefits are claimed in the importing jurisdiction
Inspection certificates, phytosanitary certificates, or conditional-export licenses required for goods subject to regulatory approval
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The GDT applies heightened post-clearance scrutiny to zero-rated exports and VAT refund applications, auditing (i) invoice-against-customs-declaration congruence, (ii) physical reality of export logistics, (iii) offshore residency and substance of the buyer, (iv) use of back-to-back SPVs to fabricate offshore consumption, and (v) repeated reliance on 180-day extensions or set-off mechanisms. If export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days (unless a lawful State Bank of Vietnam set-off/extension is obtained), the zero-rated treatment is retrospectively withdrawn: the LLC must re-output VAT at 8%/10%, refund any input VAT credit previously refunded or credited, and pay late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the underpaid tax from the original due date to full settlement. Under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP (as amended by Decree 102/2021/ND-CP), false e-invoices, inaccurate customs declarations, fraudulent refund claims, and tax evasion carry administrative fines from 20% to 100% of the understated tax amount (with a fine cap of VND 500 million for organizational misconduct) plus forcible recovery of the refund and interest. Criminal liability may attach under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015/2017: commercial legal persons found guilty of tax evasion face fines of VND 500 million to VND 20 billion, suspension of operations, or a 1-3 year prohibition on doing business; responsible managers may face imprisonment of up to 7 years, and the tax authority may publish the enterprise on its compliance blacklist, revoke the e-invoice authorization, and delegate the case to the Economic Police for criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) — the central bank and foreign exchange administration authority; all foreign exchange activities are regulated by the SBV and the Foreign Exchange Control Department, whose authority is exercised through licensed commercial banks as authorized foreign exchange institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vietnam maintains a managed partial convertibility regime. Current account transactions (trade payments, service fees, interest, and profit remittances) are generally convertible without pre-approval, subject to documentation and tax compliance. Capital account transactions (FDI capital contributions, shareholder loans, acquisitions, divestment proceeds) require prior registration with the SBV and are settled only through licensed banks via a foreign investment capital account (DICA). Profit remittance is permitted after audited financial statements and corporate income tax finalization; a tax clearance certificate may be required. The VND is not freely floatable; the SBV sets daily reference exchange rates within a trading band.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Vietnam imposes a mandatory export proceeds surrender: exporters must sell 80% of eligible export foreign currency receipts to a licensed bank within 15 days of receipt. The remaining 20% may be retained in a foreign currency account. For a PE buyout SPV with no direct export operations, any non-trade or incidental foreign receipts should be classified as capital/current-account remittances, not export proceeds; however, any indirect export-related inflows must comply with Circular 03/2016/TT-NHNN and be surrendered within the statutory 15-day window.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs are not authorized banks in Vietnam and cannot hold a DICA or corporate operational account directly. They may provide payment facilitation or IBAN-style services upstream, but the SPV must maintain its primary settlement and DICA accounts with an SBV-licensed bank. Use of an offshore EMI for VND clearing would violate SBV regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for corporate account opening. The SPV's legal representative or a director/officer holding a notarized power of attorney must appear at the bank branch in person. Remote video onboarding may supplement but not replace the initial in-person KYC interview. Some banks accept a local signatory or authorized representative with a certified POA for ongoing operations, but the opening procedure mandates direct physical verification of the legal representative or beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign investment structure with offshore private equity sponsors and no physical local office
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Investment certificate (IRC), enterprise registration certificate, lease agreement and utility bill, board resolution appointing account signatories, an organizational chart, and a detailed business plan evidencing substantive PE activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-time inbound FDI contribution from a Cayman/BVI holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SBV DICA registration confirmation, notarized capital contribution board resolutions, and trackable source-of-funds evidence from upstream investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector classification as financial / PE SPV without a local banking license
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IRC stating ISIC 6499 as holding and investment activity, a written confidentiality and regulatory compliance memorandum, and confirmation that licensed activities are not being performed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of DICA for non-investment disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-defined disbursement schedule linked to the acquisition SPA, lender drawdown notices, and contractual invoices from advisors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity due to multiple layers of offshore entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO declarations on bank forms, ownership chain charts, passport copies, and source-of-wealth or source-of-funds documentation for all 25%+ beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure in the sponsor structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory licenses of fund managers or advisers, audited fund financial statements, and FATF-compliant AML policies of the fund.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound FDI capital must be wired from the investor's overseas bank to the SPV's DICA at a licensed Vietnamese bank. SWIFT payment instructions must cite the FDI capital contribution purpose and be supported by the IRC, SBV registration code, and the bank's DICA account mandate. The bank will identify the transfer as capital injection and maintain the DICA balance until the SPV redeploys it. The capital must be used only for lawful investment purposes and must be recorded in the company's charter capital ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for acquisition consideration, syndicated loan repayment, dealer fees, and operating costs should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 / MT202 using VND or foreign exchange settlement through the operating account. For trade-related payables (e.g., equipment or services), commercial letters of credit can be used, but for a PE SPV, direct telegraphic transfers are the prevalent clearing rail. All outbound payments must be supported by underlying contracts, approved by the bank's compliance team, and reported to the SBV under the balance of payments or foreign loan monitoring system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards between a licensed Vietnamese bank and the SPV for genuine VND/USD exposure, maximum tenor one year.
FX swaps (spot/forward) with an authorized bank.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for the LBO/syndicated facility.
NDFs permitted only off-balance-sheet / offshore on an exceptional basis; not recommended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Fee Renewal (Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for going-concern enterprises; within 30 days of commencing operations for newly established entities based on charter capital tier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative fines of VND 2,000,000 – VND 20,000,000 plus persistent non-payment leading to compulsory debt enforcement and suspension of business registration activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Quyết toán thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from fiscal year-end; normally 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines escalating from VND 2,000,000 to VND 40,000,000 based on delay; underpaid tax interest at 0.03% per day; repeat non-compliance can trigger criminal referral for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Submission (Báo cáo tài chính năm)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department and Department of Planning and Investment (for foreign-invested entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from fiscal year-end; normally 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from VND 10,000,000 to VND 40,000,000 for late or non-submission; false financial statement presentation may subject management to penalties and legal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Project Implementation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province of investment registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding calendar year, except project-specific due dates stated in the Investment Registration Certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warnings and fines from VND 2,000,000 to VND 20,000,000; failure to report may result in suspension or revocation of the Investment Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Labor Use Report and Social Insurance Listing (Báo cáo tình hình sử dụng lao động)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Labor, Invalids and Social Affairs (DOLISA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; also must be filed within 05 days of any layoff-related or large workforce change in selected provinces.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from VND 1,000,000 to VND 10,000,000 for late or inaccurate reporting; for significant non-compliance, social insurance audits may be initiated.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All 100% foreign-invested enterprises, including private equity SPVs, are required to obtain an independent audit of annual financial statements, regardless of revenue, asset size, or number of employees under Decree 17/2013/ND-CP and applicable circulars. Additionally, mandatory audit applies to public-interest entities, credit institutions, insurance companies, and enterprises with 51% state ownership or other specific regulated industries.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS), applied under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; consolidated financial statements of listed parent entities are prepared using VAS and may be supplemented by IFRS only in specific permitted cases. The audited financial statements must be submitted to the tax authority, Department of Planning and Investment, and the parent-entity auditor as required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not impose a separate standalone annual UBO confirmation filing under the Enterprise Law. The foreign-invested LLC must update its register of members and file a change notice with the Department of Planning and Investment within 10 days of any transfer or change in membership, legal representatives, and ownership ratios. The company must also maintain and refresh beneficial-owner documentation for AML/sanctions screening as part of bank account annual compliance and during any notarized corporate acts; however, no government receipt is issued solely for annual UBO confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Sổ đăng ký thành viên)
Register of Legal Representatives and Management Board (Nếu có)
Minute Book and Resolution Book of the Members' Council
Book of Changes to the Enterprise Registration (Sổ theo dõi thay đổi nội dung đăng ký doanh nghiệp)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 – $1,800 (standard provider fee for registered office address, legal representative coordination, and filing support in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 – $9,000 (typical independent audit fee for a single-asset or funding vehicle SPV with no substantive operations, depending on complexity and auditor tier)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 20% CIT rate; preferential rates of 10%–15% with tax holidays up to 4 years are available only for enterprises qualifying under sectoral or locational incentive regimes such as high-tech zones, supporting industries, or large-scale industrial zones. A private equity buyout SPV ordinarily does not qualify unless it holds assets in an incentivised project and meets the revenue and employment substance conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 01/TNDN (quarterly provisional CIT return), filed electronically via the National Public Service Portal of the General Department of Taxation (https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 30 days after the end of each quarter (Q1: 30 April; Q2: 30 July; Q3: 30 October; Q4: 30 January of the following fiscal year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise identification: tax identification number, legal name, registered address, and fiscal quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete with the Vietnamese LLC’s own tax code and registered address. Non-resident parent shareholders must not be named as the filer; the LLC files as a resident enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cumulative quarterly gross revenue, including investment income, disposal gains, dividends, interest, and management-monitoring fees earned by the SPV.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Vietnam-sourced gross receipts without offsetting foreign investor-level expenses or treaty-allocated costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate deductible expenses: borrowing costs, transaction fees, professional fees, payroll, and depreciation supported by valid invoices and contemporaneous documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident service fees are deductible only if the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) has been withheld or paid; otherwise the deduction is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Preliminary taxable income and provisional CIT payable for the quarter, adjusted to reflect the annual statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If treaty relief on interest or royalties is intended, obtain the tax authority’s written confirmation before the quarterly filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late provisional returns are subject to administrative fines from VND 2 million to VND 25 million depending on the number of days overdue. Underpayment of the quarter’s provisional CIT above the final CIT due triggers late-payment interest at 0.03% per day on the shortfall.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 03/TNDN (annual finalisation CIT return), filed electronically via the National Public Service Portal of the General Department of Taxation (https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (typically 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer). Audited financial statements must be attached where the enterprise is legally required to have them audited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax code, fiscal year, contact details, and legal representative authorisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return is signed by the Vietnamese LLC’s legal representative or licensed tax agent. The non-resident shareholders do not file a separate CIT return in Vietnam.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue, non-taxable income (dividends from domestic corporate subsidiaries), and taxable revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Vietnam-source revenue of the SPV is taxable; foreign-source portfolio income that is not attributable to a Vietnamese permanent establishment is out of scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses, depreciation, interest expense, transaction costs, and disallowances (non-deductible losses, FCT adjustments, thinning-capitalisation interest).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign related parties are deductible only when they satisfy arm’s length conditions and the payer has obtained the relevant FCT documentation or treaty-resident certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses brought forward, used, and remaining, limited to a 5-year carryforward horizon.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Vietnamese LLC cannot be shared or absorbed at the foreign parent or any other group entity; only the Vietnamese taxpayer may use its own carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss offsets, the applied statutory CIT rate, and gross CIT payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are not available in the Vietnam return for taxes paid by a non-resident shareholder; any treaty credit application must be raised through the applicable DTA mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly provisional CIT previously paid, total final CIT payable, additional tax due, and any refund amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is paid in VND to the LLC’s Vietnam bank account; direct set-off against foreign shareholder liabilities is not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 03/TNDN carries an administrative fine of up to VND 25 million; any unpaid CIT accrues late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. A return found to be fraudulent or grossly non-compliant triggers an additional penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax, plus disclosure to the tax fraud unit for criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Vietnam does not impose a withholding tax on dividend distributions declared from after-tax profits to foreign shareholders; the LLC remits after-tax profits in accordance with the Investment Law and foreign exchange regulations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although the domestic dividend withholding rate is nil, a foreign beneficial owner claiming DTA protection for interest, royalties, or capital gains must submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), a statutory declaration of beneficial ownership, and the relevant treaty-relief form to the Vietnamese tax authority before the payment date. The Vietnamese withholding payer applies the reduced treaty rate only after receiving the Vietnamese tax branch’s written confirmation; retrospective treaty relief may also be claimed through a refund procedure under Circular 205/2013/TT-BTC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates under the Foreign Contractor Tax regime: interest income 5% CIT on gross proceeds (VAT exempt); intellectual-property royalties 10% CIT plus 5% VAT, producing a 15% aggregate withholding on gross royalties. Under Vietnam’s double tax agreements, interest rates are commonly reduced to 5%–10% and royalties to 5%–10%, provided the foreign recipient is the beneficial owner and has met the TRC and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File where annual revenue exceeds VND 50 billion OR related-party transaction value exceeds VND 30 billion; Master File is required where the consolidated worldwide revenue of the ultimate parent entity exceeds VND 500 billion. Vietnamese TP reporting also requires a Country-by-Country notification for consolidated groups above VND 18,000 billion (approx. USD 685 million); enterprises below these thresholds must still maintain contemporaneous TP documentation and perform an arm’s length analysis.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not codify an ESR regime equivalent to the Gulf Cooperation Council’s Economic Substance Regulations. However, an Economic Substance Doctrine is applied through the general anti-abuse rules in Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, the test of ‘business purpose’ in tax-treaty interpretation, and the constitutional requirement that an enterprise be a genuine operating entity with headquarters, managerial decision-making, payroll, and accounting records in Vietnam. A private equity buyout SPV must demonstrate real substance by maintaining a physical office, local management, transaction controls, and contemporaneous records of the investment and acquisition decisions; absence of substance can justify recharacterisation of the SPV’s roles, denial of treaty benefits, and a full 20% CIT recalculation on the allocable profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally understating gross revenue, reporting false portfolio-disposal gains, issuing or accepting counterfeit VAT invoices, or fabricating artificial deductible expenses related to the PE buyout transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of 1 to 3 times the evaded CIT for underdeclared income; late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; criminal prosecution for tax evasion where the unpaid amount is VND 100,000,000 or more, with imprisonment of up to 3 years, or up to 10 years when the amount exceeds VND 500,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil is available where directors knowingly sign fraudulent returns or direct the concealment of revenue; directors and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution, suffer travel bans, and can be sentenced to imprisonment under the Penal Code for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a nominee-controlled SPV with no staffing, no Vietnamese premises, no decision-making records, and using the SPV conductive channel to divert equity gains to a foreign related party, stripping value from the Vietnam tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard the shell entity under the general anti-abuse rule, reattribute income to the underlying beneficial owner, deny preferential rates, impose a reassessment at the 20% CIT rate, add late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and apply a non-compliance penalty of up to 3 times the underpaid amount; substantial violations also risk enterprise licence suspension under commercial law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly establish or maintain a sham SPV expose themselves to personal liability for the deficient tax and interest, a travel ban, and criminal charges for the use of false commercial documents, notwithstanding the general limited-liability protection of the legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT non-compliance in cross-border financial flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using syndicated-loan wires or SWIFT payment systems without developing KYC files, failing to identify beneficial owners, or omitting to report large transactions at the VND 300 million threshold as required by the Law on Anti-Money Laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines in the range of VND 50,000,000 to VND 200,000,000 for non-reporting; repeat violations can lead to suspension of the entity’s payment or investment licences; wilful concealment of the economic nature of a wire constitutes money laundering with a criminal penalty of up to 10 years’ imprisonment and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who circumvent AML controls, falsify beneficial-ownership declarations, or knowingly route funds to avoid detection are personally liable, risk civil forfeiture of personal assets, may be banned from overseas travel, and may be prosecuted for money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing documentation failure and mispricing of related-entity services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File/Master File when turnover exceeds VND 50 billion and related-party dealings exceed VND 30 billion; electing a baseless arm’s length method (e.g., unsupported TNMM) for acquisition management fees, monitoring fees, or carrying-interest allocations, or economically mischaracterising the SPV’s risk exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of deemed turnover and recharacterisation of the SPV’s transaction, recalculation of the CIT deficiency at 20%, late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, and an administrative penalty ranging from 20% to 100% of the transfer-pricing adjustment amount; treaty benefits may also be disallowed under Limitation-on-Benefits provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are held personally liable when they knowingly sign false TP declarations or deliberately destroy contemporaneous documents; such conduct constitutes wilful negligence, leading to joint restitution obligations, travel restrictions, and possible imprisonment for fraudulent tax administration.
